subject.title: [Feature]: Expose before_tool_call/after_tool_call in internal hooks system

question: Should managed `HOOK.md` hooks become a second blocking and parameter-rewriting tool-policy surface, or should enforceable tool policy remain exclusive to typed plugins?
rationale: Both directions are technically possible, but the choice changes a security-sensitive extension boundary and cannot be safely inferred from community demand alone; current documentation favors typed plugins while prior discussion retained this issue for an explicit decision.

options.title: Preserve the typed-plugin boundary
options.body: Keep managed hooks side-effect-only, reject unsupported tool-policy event declarations clearly, and direct reusable enforcement policies to installable ClawHub plugins.

options.title: Design a managed policy bridge
options.body: Specify and implement managed before/after tool events with plugin-equivalent ordering, blocking, parameter mutation, approval, timeout, failure, and cross-runtime coverage guarantees.

recommendation.title: Preserve the typed-plugin boundary
recommendation.body: Keep managed hooks side-effect-only, reject unsupported tool-policy event declarations clearly, and direct reusable enforcement policies to installable ClawHub plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history introduced the managed hook surface and their discussion comment retained this as the canonical product/API decision.
